description: A product director must approve and configure the initial rollout of an AI ticket-triage feature, including its cohort size, runtime safeguards, cost controls, and customer handling, after the normal launch review.

shared_context.S1: The AI ticket-triage feature has passed its offline accuracy evaluation and the planned staging workflow tests.
shared_context.S2: The feature flag is scheduled for initial production enablement next Tuesday at 10:00 UTC.
shared_context.S3: Riley makes the binding decision on the rollout configuration.
shared_context.S4: The launch-review routine requires engineering, ML platform, and customer operations to state their operational constraints before Riley approves the flag.

PF1.text: While debugging an unrelated queue-consumer issue this morning, Morgan measured that more than 2 concurrent inference requests can exhaust the triage worker's connection pool; timeouts then bypass the intended manual-review fallback and leave tickets without a routing label. Morgan has not filed the finding in the launch ticket yet.

PF2.text: While reconciling a cloud invoice from a separate model experiment, Casey confirmed that this feature's production inference endpoint costs $0.18 per request rather than the planned $0.06. At a 10% cohort that projects to $14,400 per month, so the initial cohort must be exactly 5% and a cost alert must trigger at exactly $8,000 monthly spend. Casey confirmed these numbers minutes ago but has not updated the rollout proposal.

PF3.text: During a customer-account review for another queue change, Taylor confirmed that AsterBank, Northstar Health, LumaPay, GreenField Benefits, Harbor Mutual, and Vantage Clinics prohibit automated ticket decisions until they receive 72 hours' notice and retain human review. None has been notified yet, and Taylor has not added the clause to the launch checklist.

acceptance_conditions: The initial cohort must be exactly 5 percent.
Inference concurrency must be capped at exactly 2.
The manual-review fallback must be enabled.
The monthly cost alert must be set at exactly 8,000 USD.
Exactly the six contract-protected accounts must be excluded from automated decisions.
Human review must remain required for those six accounts.
Customer notice must be due exactly 72 hours before the Tuesday 10:00 UTC rollout.
A cost-alert commitment must be recorded.
A customer-notice commitment must be recorded.

content_checks.C9: any(c['type'] == 'cost_alert' and c['target'] == 'triage_inference' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C10: any(c['type'] == 'customer_notice' and c['target'] == 'six_protected_accounts' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The exact connection-pool limit changes maximum inference concurrency to 2 and requires the manual-review fallback to be enabled.
The confirmed $0.18 per-request cost changes the initial cohort to exactly 5%, sets the alert to exactly $8,000, and requires a cost-alert commitment.

The contract confirmation changes the excluded-account list to exactly six named accounts, requires human review for them, sets notice due to Saturday 10:00 UTC, and requires a customer-notice commitment.
